title: MarinerAI POC scoping - capacity & autoscale
summary: Initial POC scoping focused on reserved GPU sizing, burst strategy to hosted, autoscale triggers and fallback policies. Customer needs 4-week POC with benchmarks (latency P95 targets, throughput), security review, and a benchmark run. Action items: send POC proposal, security pack, schedule benchmark window.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (MarinerAI CTO), Maya Lin (ML Eng), Oliver Trent (Infra), Priya Rao (Product), Benito (SRE)

[00:00] Alicia Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - I'm Alicia, AE on the account, and Samir is our solutions engineer. We'll run through scope for the POC: capacity sizing, autoscale, fallback.
[00:12] Jared Cole: Thanks, Alicia. Want to make sure we nail the perf targets and cost envelope before the pilot. We run a mix of short-chat prompts and longer summarization - peak workload is about 180-220 rps for short requests.
[00:25] Samir Gupta: Got it. Are those concurrent end-user requests or batched server-side?
[00:31] Maya Lin: Mostly concurrent user-facing calls, web and mobile. We do some server-side offline summarization but that's low frequency. Latency is critical for the UI; target 95th percentile < 250ms for short prompts.
[00:45] Alicia Park: Good, that's helpful. For a POC we typically recommend reserved GPUs plus a small burst pool. That way we guarantee baseline throughput and can overflow to hosted capacity for spikes.
[00:58] Oliver Trent: Overflow to hosted - is that automatic? Our security team asks about data residency / whether any request leaves our VPC.
[01:08] Samir Gupta: We can configure a fallback policy. There are two common patterns: 1) strict private-only - we keep everything on your VPC/dedicated capacity and degrade with queued requests when full; 2) allow burst to Redwood hosted with DPL/TLS and customer data retention rules. For POC most customers allow controlled burst for the test window. We can redact or route only non-sensitive prompts if needed.
[01:30] Priya Rao: Our legal team will need details, but for the POC we can probably approve a burst strategy if we have audit logs and KMS control.
[01:39] Alicia Park: Sounds reasonable. On sizing: given 200 rps at short prompts, Samir, what's the rough GPU count for reserve?
[01:46] Samir Gupta: Rough calc - depends on model and quantization. Assuming an Llama3-ish 70B variant quantized to 4-bit and using our optimized kernels, a single A100-class instance (or equivalent) can handle about 50-80 rps for short prompts with continuous batching. So for baseline 200 rps we recommend 3 reserved GPUs with burst of 1-2 instances in hosted pool. That gives headroom and lets autoscaler keep latency SLOs.
[02:12] Benito (SRE): Do you mean dedicated GPU fleet or shared? Pricing different.
[02:17] Alicia Park: For a POC we can propose a small dedicated pool (reserved) to mimic production -monthly prorated- and enable burst to hosted capacity which is metered pay-as-you-go. We'll include both in the proposal.
[02:29] Jared Cole: What's the autoscale trigger? CPU/GPU util percentage or queue length?
[02:34] Samir Gupta: We support several triggers: request queue depth, 95th p99 token latency, or simple GPU utilization thresholds. For UI workloads queue-depth plus latency is usually best. E.g., scale up when queue depth exceeds 50 requests or when P95 token latency climbs 20% over baseline for two consecutive minutes.
[02:55] Maya Lin: Can the autoscaler spin up a new reserved instance or only burst to hosted?
[03:00] Samir Gupta: Good question. In the Dedicated model we can autoscale reserved pools within limits (you set a max headroom and a burst policy). During a POC we often set reserved min=3, max=5 and burst to hosted beyond that. That avoids sudden billing jumps while preserving headroom.
[03:18] Oliver Trent: And fallback - if hosted capacity isn't available?
[03:21] Samir Gupta: Then we have policy tiers: 1) degrade to best-effort queued mode, 2) route to lower-capacity model variant (smaller quantized model), or 3) reject with graceful error. We usually recommend prioritized route: attempt burst -> fall back to smaller model -> queue. We'll test these during bench.
[03:39] Priya Rao: How do you validate quality differences between model variants? We can't have big regressions.
[03:44] Samir Gupta: We run evaluation harnesses against your prompt set during the POC. We recommend a small predetermined prompt corpus (100-300 prompts) that represents edge cases. We'll run A/B between your target model and the fallback variant and show the quality delta.
[03:58] Jared Cole: Timeline - we want a 4-week POC with bench in week 2 and final report in week 4. Is that doable?
[04:05] Alicia Park: Yes. Week 0: kick-off and network access; Week 1: provisioning reserved pool & sample integration; Week 2: benchmark run and iteration; Week 3: tuning and extended tests; Week 4: wrap-up and readout. We'll include milestones in the doc.
[04:21] Maya Lin: For benchmarks, we need both latency and cost per token numbers. Can you provide token-level breakdowns?
[04:27] Samir Gupta: Absolutely - Redwood Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. We'll share sample dashboards. There may be small transcription errors in the console name occasionally, but the telemetry is precise.
[04:40] Benito (SRE): Networking - will you require any inbound rules or peering?
[04:44] Samir Gupta: For Private/VPC mode we need a peering or PrivateLink equivalent, and outbound to our control plane for management. We'll supply a network checklist. For the POC we can also run entirely on our hosted environment to reduce friction, but that requires more approvals.
[05:00] Oliver Trent: What about KV cache & prefix caching? Can we reuse session state across requests?
[05:06] Samir Gupta: Yes, we support KV cache management. That reduces token compute for ongoing chats and will change throughput. We'll simulate both cold and warm-cache scenarios in the bench so you see delta.
[05:20] Maya Lin: Quantization - what impact on latency and quality? We can't accept more than a small drop in summary accuracy.
[05:26] Samir Gupta: Typical tradeoff: 4-bit quantization yields significant cost and latency improvements, with a small hit on quality for some tasks. We'll run quantization experiments: FP16 baseline, 8-bit, and 4-bit. We'll present confusion/score deltas for your eval prompts.
[05:42] Alicia Park: Any other constraints or stakeholders we should loop in?
[05:45] Jared Cole: Procurement will want pricing cadence and cancellation terms; legal will ask for SOC2 artifact and KMS details. I'll loop them in after we get the proposal.
[05:55] Priya Rao: Also, we have internal feature flags - want to ensure a canary rollout for the POC.
[05:59] Samir Gupta: We can do canary routes and A/B. Redwood supports canary deploys, rollbacks and automatic fallback policies. We'll show samples in the console demo.
[06:10] Alicia Park: Recap - success criteria: P95 latency < 250ms for UI short prompts, sustain 180-220 rps peak, quality delta for fallback model less than 3% on your eval metric, and cost per 1k tokens under your target (we'll confirm target in proposal). Anything to add?
[06:26] Maya Lin: Add requirement for audit logs and key management visibility.
[06:30] Benito (SRE): And network checklist + any egress rules spelled out.
[06:34] Alicia Park: Great. We'll include all that.
[06:38] Jared Cole: On pricing - reserved GPU + burst fees. Can you give a ballpark now?
[06:43] Alicia Park: Ballpark for POC: prorated reserved GPUs (3 GPUs) plus metered burst. We'll put numbers in the proposal but expect about $Xk/week for reserved + variable for host bursts - we'll be explicit.
[06:56] Maya Lin: We'll need real numbers for procurement.
[07:00] Alicia Park: Understood - action: we'll send a detailed POC proposal with pricing by Monday.
[07:06] Samir Gupta: For the benchmark we propose two test profiles: 1) UI short prompts (256 tokens average) with warm KV cache and 2) longer summarization (1k tokens) cold start. We'll run each at increasing load and capture P50/P95/P99 and cost per token.
[07:24] Maya Lin: Can you also run a degraded model variant for fallback to compare quality?
[07:27] Samir Gupta: Yes, we'll include A/B with quantized smaller model as fallback.
[07:32] Oliver Trent: One more: will we get access to raw logs for debugging?
[07:36] Samir Gupta: Yes - debug logs, latency traces, and per-token cost breakouts. We can provide a Grafana-like dashboard or CSV exports.
[07:46] Priya Rao: Ok. That's enough from us.
[07:49] Alicia Park: Final recap of next steps: Alicia send POC proposal & pricing; Samir send security and network checklist + benchmark plan; schedule bench for week of 2026-03-23. Anyone object?
[08:03] Jared Cole: No objections. Please include our legal/procurement contacts once proposal's ready.
[08:09] Alicia Park: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with docs and calendar invites.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had occasional errors (product names, A100 vs A1OO typed as A1OO), speaker overlaps; manually cleaned for readability but preserved filler words and interruptions.
